speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You've mentioned a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache; to help narrow this down, how long have these symptoms been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Scarlet fever (caused by Group A Streptococcus).

The clinical picture of a recent viral-like prodrome (fever, rhinorrhea, headache) followed by a pruritic rash that spares the perioral area is highly suggestive of scarlet fever. I will request a throat culture and a complete blood count to confirm the diagnosis.
